scope: SDL_SetLogOutputFunction and SDL_SetMainReady for the synchronous single-owner native SDL backend; not general asynchronous logging or video/audio lifecycle support.
implementation: SDL receives one registered native trampoline and host-owned state; guest function address and userdata remain uint32 values.
A live owner-thread allocator/CPU frame is required before reading callback state. Worker or out-of-frame logging stops.
Messages shorter than 1 MiB are copied into temporary guest heap memory, dispatched cdecl with userdata/category/priority/message, and freed after return.
The allocator frame is suspended around guest dispatch so supported nested SDL entries use their own CPU/frame.
LastError is restored. Existing callback machinery copies the CPU, preserves general registers, verifies cdecl stack cleanup, and retains guest FP thread state.
NULL disables logging according to the pinned SDL behavior; replacing callbacks preserves supplied guest userdata.
SDL_SetMainReady calls the actual SDL 3.2.18 lifecycle function, recording its native main-thread identity; repeated calls preserve the original identity.
limits: No callback from native worker threads without an established guest context.
No nonlocal guest exit through a native SDL logger frame.
Temporary message allocation failure or overlong message remains an explicit diagnostic stop.
No SDL_GetLogOutputFunction/default-function guest API, generic vararg logger, native window or event-loop implementation.
tests: Native SDL_LogMessage invokes the installed guest callback; normal/TSan/both-guard Mac and sole guarded iPad tests cover copied UTF8 and long messages, reentry, replacement/NULL, CPU/stack and LastError, plus Mac boundary fault cases. Main-ready is invoked twice through its emitted void/cdecl ABI. Eighteen Mac fault cases include incorrect fixed-parameter count for variadic SDL_LogMessage; the only admitted native log format is literal %s with one host-owned message.
